Turner explicitly notes collision with púruṣa and shortening under kinship/address use, providing independent alternatives to simple sound change. Kalkoti 2023 meéš is a notable late-High case, not predicted merely by Palula early ee.

analysis: Gilgit maáran ‘death’ has late newly long aa in the first syllable, with a following short syllable. The action-noun suffix and its r/n consonants distinguish it from the monosyllabic new-length cases; no obvious historical cluster directly explains the length. Old accent is unknown, so it remains an independent morphology/quantity problem rather than an inherited-accent exception.

analysis: Gilgit maristán ‘unpaid worker, slave’ accents the final short syllable. The servant-plus-position compound and shortening of old sthāna provide independent structural information. The accents of márya and sthā́na cannot simply be assigned to the whole reconstructed compound.

The broad family contains independently accented variants with different extensions, including mástaka and mastíṣka. Only the actual immediate formation can supply an old prediction; brain terminology is not one undifferentiated reflex of masta.

analysis: Palula mháalu has early aa, whereas Gilgit/Kohistani maálo and Guresi maálu have late aa; uncle forms moól/mahuúl differ further. VhV contraction and kinship morphology independently distinguish this from simple early extended adjectives. Strand's agnates form mhâlayʹa and father-and-son compound have additional morphology and cannot be pooled with father. Kundal mā̌l supplies a source-specific rising mark.

analysis: Palula maac̣huríi and Strand mâc̣hurʹî accent early long final ii after a long unaccented first root syllable. The compound with maker material and a feminine ending independently distinguishes this from a simple fly noun. Parent mākṣiká and kará do not fix the old whole-word accent, and Shina unmarked variants are only segmental comparators.

analysis: Gilgit maáni ‘pearl’ has late aa before i. The independently reconstructed long-vowel collection derivative and loss of y distinguish it from parent maṇí. This is a potential contracted i-noun counterpart to other late-long forms, but the old accent of the derivative is unknown.

analysis: Palula méeši/Strand mʹêši has early long ee before the feminine ending after contraction of a maternal-aunt compound. This should be compared with phéepi ‘paternal aunt’ as a kinship/gender class, not as direct retention of either mātŕ̥ or svásr̥ accent. Kalkoti meeš lacks final i and requires explicit source tone evidence.

analysis: Palula móonu/Strand mʹôno has early long oo before u/o, with raising compatible with an old long ā. Skin bag, churn and ghee bag are related uses of the same object. The old vessel etymology is explicitly uncertain and cannot import the accent of unrelated mā́na ‘measure’ merely through surface similarity.

analysis: Palula maamaá/Strand mâmâʹ ‘mother's brother’ has final late aa, while Gilgit máamo and Astori móomo have early first-root prominence before o; Kohistani mamáa has final early aa. Strand mʹômo and Kalkoti maam denote the mother's father instead. Kinship relation and gender/declension must therefore precede cross-language accent comparison.
